Obstructive shock.systolic_BP: Systolic BP < 90 mmHg or vasopressors required to achieve a BP ≥ 90 mmHg despite adequate filling status.
Obstructive shock.and: End-organ hypoperfusion (altered mental status; cold, clammy skin; oliguria/anuria; increased serum lactate).

Persistent hypotension.systolic_BP: Systolic BP < 90 mmHg or systolic BP drop ≥ 40 mmHg, lasting longer than 15 min and not caused by new-onset arrhythmia, hypovolaemia, or sepsis.

diagnosis_section.summary: Increased awareness of venous thromboembolic disease and wider availability of non-invasive imaging (mainly CT pulmonary angiography, CTPA) has led to more frequent diagnostic workups for pulmonary embolism (PE). Contemporary PE confirmation rates in diagnostic workups may be as low as ~5% in recent North American studies versus ~50% in the early 1980s. Non-invasive diagnostic strategies must safely exclude PE in low pre-test probability populations; conversely, a positive test should have adequate specificity to justify anticoagulant treatment.
